plan: Store the workspace as a deep-copied plain-dict tree; deep-copy again on to_data() so no caller ever aliases internal state.
Implement one recursive generator _walk(items, depth) yielding (item, depth); build total_word_count, unresolved_markers, and outline as simple folds over it so containment rules live in one place.

Handle markers with a compiled regex \[\[\?(\w+)\]\]: strip them (replacing with a space) before counting words via \b\w+\b, and capture their identifiers for unresolved_markers alongside reference 'unresolved' lists; dedupe with a set and sort.
Render outline as workspace title plus one line per walked item, indented two spaces per nesting level (top-level items at level 1 under the title), formatted '<kind>: <title>'.

Implement move with a strict validate-then-mutate protocol: check id types, locate item and destination, reject non-container destinations, reject destination being the item or any descendant (identity comparison), and bounds-check the index — all before pop/insert — so any ValueError leaves to_data() byte-identical.
Resolve the literal destination_id 'workspace' to the root item list; index=None appends, otherwise insert at the validated index.
mechanisms: Single recursive tree-walk generator shared by all read operations
Per-kind dispatch for summary contributions (note text parsing vs. reference declared counts)
Regex marker stripping before word tokenization
Validate-then-mutate move protocol for atomic failure semantics
Identity-based (object 'is') containment check for self/descendant rejection
Deep-copy isolation at both construction and export boundaries
